document: [OVERVIEW] Infosys at a glance (as of Oct 2026): Infosys Limited is an Indian multinational IT services, digital and consulting company headquartered in Bengaluru, Karnataka. It describes itself as a global leader in AI-first business consulting and technology services. Infosys is present in 59 countries, has 328K+ employees, serves about 2,027 clients, and has more than 40 years of operating history.
title: Infosys at a glance

document: Its last-twelve-month revenue is roughly US$20.3-20.4 billion (LTM to Q2 FY27, the company's own pages differ slightly). Its market capitalisation is about US$42 billion per the company history page. Infosys is listed on the BSE (code 500209), NSE (INFY) and NYSE (ADS: INFY), and is a constituent of the BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty 50. It is generally counted among India's Big Six IT companies.
title: Infosys at a glance

document: [OVERVIEW] Infosys purpose, values and brand positioning (as of Oct 2026): Infosys' stated purpose is to amplify human potential and create the next opportunity for people, businesses and communities. Its core values are abbreviated CLIFE: Client value, Leadership by example, Integrity and transparency, Fairness, and Excellence.
title: Infosys purpose, values and brand positioning

document: Its brand tagline-style messaging is 'Navigate your next'. The company says it enables clients to navigate digital transformation powered by cloud and AI, with an AI-first core, agile digital at scale, and always-on learning. Employees are called 'Infoscions'. Infosys' website has an AI assistant called Leon ('Ask Leon').
title: Infosys purpose, values and brand positioning

document: [OVERVIEW] Naming and corporate identity history (as of Oct 2026): Infosys was incorporated as Infosys Consultants Private Limited in Pune on 2 July 1981.
title: Naming and corporate identity history

document: It was known as Infosys Consultants until 1992, then Infosys Technologies (1992-2011), and has been called Infosys Limited since 2011. ISIN is INE009A01021. The par value of an equity share is Rs 5.
title: Naming and corporate identity history

document: [OVERVIEW] Founding of Infosys (1981) (as of Oct 2026): Infosys was founded on 2 July 1981 in Pune by N. R. Narayana Murthy and six other engineers, with initial capital of US$250. The seven founders were N. R. Narayana Murthy, Nandan M. Nilekani, S. (Kris) Gopalakrishnan, S. D. (Shibulal) Shibulal, K. Dinesh, N. S. Raghavan and Ashok Arora.
title: Founding of Infosys (1981)

document: Ashok Arora left in 1989 and sold his shares to the other co-founders. The first client was Data Basics Corporation in New York. The corporate headquarters moved to Bangalore in 1983 and to Electronic City, Bangalore in 1994. In the 1980s Infosys briefly made hardware such as telex machines. Its offshore software development business grew after India's 1991 economic liberalisation.
title: Founding of Infosys (1981)

document: [OVERVIEW] Infosys history timeline 1981-2005 (as of Oct 2026): 1981 founded in Pune; 1983 HQ moves to Bangalore; 1987 first international office in Boston; 1993 IPO (Feb 1993 at Rs 95 per share, undersubscribed, Morgan Stanley stabilised it), ESOP programme introduced, ISO 9001/TickIT certification; 1994 HQ to Electronic City; 1995 first European office (UK) and development centres at Toronto and Mangalore, Bancs2000 banking package; 1996 Infosys Foundation established; 1997 CMM Level 4; 1998 Enterprise Solutions practice;
title: Infosys history timeline 1981-2005

document: 1999 listed on NASDAQ (March 1999, first Indian company on NASDAQ), reached US$100 million revenue, 21st company worldwide with CMM Level 5, Finacle core banking launched; 2000 revenue US$200 million; 2002 Nandan Nilekani becomes CEO, Progeon (now Infosys BPM) launched, Wharton Infosys Business Transformation Awards; 2003 subsidiaries in China and Australia, Thiruvananthapuram centre; 2004 revenue crosses US$1 billion, Infosys Consulting launched; 2005 largest international equity offering from India (US$1 billion).
title: Infosys history timeline 1981-2005

document: [OVERVIEW] Infosys history timeline 2006-2017 (as of Oct 2026): 2006 Infosys turns 25, 50,000+ employees, revenue doubles to US$2 billion (23 years for the first billion, 23 months for the second); Narayana Murthy turns 60 and steps back. 2007 Kris Gopalakrishnan becomes CEO; Nilekani co-chairman. 2008 revenue above US$4 billion, annual net profit above US$1 billion. 2009 100,000+ employees; member of The Global Dow. 2010 revenue above US$5 billion. 2011 Murthy hands chairmanship to K. V. Kamath; S. D. Shibulal becomes CEO; revenue above US$6 billion; 125,000+ staff. 2012 listed on NYSE;
title: Infosys history timeline 2006-2017

document: acquires Lodestone (Switzerland). 2013 Murthy returns as Executive Chairman; trades on NYSE Euronext London and Paris. 2014 Vishal Sikka becomes CEO (first outsider CEO); revenue above INR 50,000 crore. 2015 acquires Panaya, Skava, Noah Consulting; US$250 million Innovate in India Fund; dividend payout up to 50%. 2016 revenue reaches US$10 billion LTM; Infosys Mana/Nia launched. 2017 Sikka resigns in August; U. B. Pravin Rao becomes interim CEO; Nandan Nilekani returns as non-executive chairman; Salil Parekh appointed CEO effective 2 Jan 2018; Rs 13,000 crore buyback completed; payout policy up to 70% of free cash flow.
title: Infosys history timeline 2006-2017

document: [LEADERSHIP] CEO succession: Ashiss Kumar Dash named CEO-designate (as of 23 Jul 2026): On 23 July 2026, alongside Q1 FY27 results, the Infosys board appointed Ashiss Kumar Dash as CEO-designate. He is planned to succeed Salil Parekh as Managing Director and CEO on 1 April 2027, subject to shareholder approval, after Parekh completes his second term (which began 28 June 2023 and ends 31 March 2027, over nine years as CEO in total). The board has proposed a five-year term for Dash. Chairman Nandan Nilekani said the board wanted a leader who combines bold transformation with Infosys' values and customer trust, and was pleased to pick an internal leader.
title: CEO succession: Ashiss Kumar Dash named CEO-designate

document: Parekh said he took Infosys from about $10 billion to over $20 billion revenue over his two terms. Dash is 54, an IIT Kharagpur chemical engineering B.Tech, has nearly 30 years at Infosys, currently serves as EVP and Global Head of Services, Utilities, Resources, Energy and Enterprise Sustainability, sits on the boards of Infosys Public Services and MRE Consulting, and completed the Stanford Global Leadership Program and London Business School Senior Executive Program. Between now and April 2027 he works alongside Parekh on the transition.
title: CEO succession: Ashiss Kumar Dash named CEO-designate

document: [FINANCIALS] FY27 guidance revision (Oct 2026) (as of 23 Oct 2026): On 23 October 2026 Infosys cut FY27 constant-currency revenue growth guidance to 1-2% (from 1.5-3%, originally 1.5-3.5% in April 2026) while keeping operating margin guidance at 20-22%.
title: FY27 guidance revision (Oct 2026)

document: Management cited softer volumes, pricing pressure and high competitive intensity, AI-driven productivity deflation, higher offshoring, cautious discretionary spend, and weakness in retail and high tech (including the ramp-down of a large automotive client noted by analysts). US-listed shares fell about 6.6% after the announcement; the stock was reported down about 29% year-to-date at that time on the Indian exchange.
title: FY27 guidance revision (Oct 2026)

document: [FINANCIALS] Q2 FY27 operations: headcount, utilisation, attrition, margins (as of 23 Oct 2026): Q2 FY27: Infosys added about 4,000 net employees, including about 8,000 college graduates, and remains on track to hire around 20,000 freshers in FY27. Utilisation was 85% and attrition about 13%. The US employee mix is majority local hires, which management said insulates it from H-1B/PERM changes. Margin bridge: post-sale customer support -70 bps, acquisition amortisation -20 bps, currency +40 bps, working days +20 bps, Project Maximus cost programme +20 bps, net flat at 21%.
title: Q2 FY27 operations: headcount, utilisation, attrition, margins

document: Subcontracting costs were 8.9% of revenue. Growth was led by financial services, energy and utilities, and manufacturing; retail and high tech lagged; North America remained soft while Europe and rest of world did well. Project Maximus is Infosys' ongoing cost-optimisation programme (not to be confused with other companies' projects of the same name). Management said AI spending is largely net new, for example AI-led legacy modernisation.
title: Q2 FY27 operations: headcount, utilisation, attrition, margins

document: [OPERATIONS] Campuses and global footprint (as of 2024-2026): Infosys' headquarters are in Electronic City, Bengaluru. Major Indian campuses include Bengaluru, Pune, Mysuru, Chennai (Mahindra World City), Thiruvananthapuram, Hyderabad, Mangalore and others.
title: Campuses and global footprint

document: International presence includes development centres and offices across the US (including a Milwaukee delivery centre opened in 2012), Canada (Toronto, Calgary), UK, Germany, Netherlands, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Australia, China, Japan, UAE and Singapore. As of Mar 2024: 94 sales and marketing offices and 139 development centres. Infosys closed down its Moscow operation after Russia's invasion of Ukraine (administrative staff only by Nov 2022).
title: Campuses and global footprint

document: [PEOPLE] Employees, hiring and culture (as of 2026): Infosys had 328,594 employees at 31 March 2026 (about 328K+ per the website). Attrition was around 12.6% in Q4 FY26 and about 13% in Q2 FY27. Women were 39.3% of staff in FY24. Plan for FY27: hire about 20,000 freshers, wage revisions in October and January. Infosys dropped its formal dress code in mid-2015.

document: [PEOPLE] Infosys Springboard, Foundation and Science Foundation (as of 2026): Infosys Springboard is Infosys' flagship free digital learning platform for digital skills, emerging technologies and life skills, delivered with curriculum partners, non-profits and educational institutions (examples: Southwark Council in the UK, digital learning centres in Ukraine with Street Child).
title: Infosys Springboard, Foundation and Science Foundation

document: [ESG] Infosys ESG vision and carbon neutrality (as of 2026): Infosys announced ESG Vision 2030 in 2020 with measurable targets across Environment, Social and Governance; its refreshed vision aims to move from carbon neutral to climate positive by 2030. It attained carbon neutrality in 2020, 30 years ahead of the Paris accord target, and publishes annual carbon neutrality declarations (ISO 14068-1) from 2020 to 2026.
title: Infosys ESG vision and carbon neutrality

document: Reports: 'Unlock Value, Responsibly' ESG Report 2025-26. ESG priorities are Environmental (preserve the planet through technology), Social (development of people) and Governance (serve all stakeholders by leading through core values). Infosys also offers Infosys Sustainability Services to clients.
title: Infosys ESG vision and carbon neutrality

document: [RISK] Legal and regulatory controversies (as of 2013-2026): Visa matters: in 2011-2012 allegations of B-1 visa misuse led to a US investigation, settled in October 2013 with a US$34 million payment without admission of guilt; in December 2019 Infosys paid US$800,000 to California over B-1/H-1B misclassification and payroll taxes (2006-2017, ~500 employees). Government portals: MCA21 (2013 onward), GSTN (2020 summons to executives) and the Income Tax e-filing portal (June 2021 launch glitches led to a summons for CEO Salil Parekh and extension of tax-filing dates).
title: Legal and regulatory controversies

document: Employee time-tracking software drew criticism in 2013. In July 2026 French labour authority DRIEETS Ile-de-France fined Infosys EUR 175,000 over a non-compliant working-time recording system. In June 2026 hiring assessments for over 20,000 trainee candidates were paused after impersonation and malpractice. The 2022 Russia-presence scrutiny involved Infosys' Moscow office.
title: Legal and regulatory controversies

document: [RISK] Business risks and market narrative 2026 (as of Oct 2026): Key themes in 2026 coverage: AI-driven productivity deflation and clients demanding lower prices; soft discretionary demand in North America; weakness in retail and high tech; competitive pricing; weak H2 FY27 outlook with sequential growth guided slightly negative to flat;

document: large deal ramp in FY28; wage hikes pressuring margins offset by Project Maximus; currency tailwind from rupee depreciation; Indian IT stocks under pressure from AI disruption fears, which Infosys countered via Topaz Fabric and its Anthropic partnership.
